definitions.explanation: A scene or view at a particular place, especially one with emotional or atmospheric significance. Used in literary and formal contexts.

examples.japanese: {美|うつく}しい{場景|ばけい}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: A beautiful scene spread out before us.

examples.japanese: {小説|しょうせつ}の{冒頭|ぼうとう}の{場景|ばけい}が{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
examples.english: The opening scene of the novel was memorable.

examples.japanese: {戦後|せんご}の{焼|や}け{野原|のはら}の{場景|ばけい}は{多|おお}くの{作家|さっか}に{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: The scene of the postwar burnt-out wasteland influenced many writers.

notes:
A somewhat literary or formal word for a scene or setting, composed of {場|ば} (place) and {景|けい} (scenery, view). More evocative than the everyday word {場面|ばめん}, emphasizing the visual or atmospheric quality of a scene.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {美|うつく}しい{場景|ばけい} — beautiful scene
- {印象的|いんしょうてき}な{場景|ばけい} — memorable scene
- {壮大|そうだい}な{場景|ばけい} — grand spectacle
- {場景|ばけい}が{広|ひろ}がる — a scene unfolds

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {場面|ばめん} — scene (more common, used for specific moments in stories or events)
- {光景|こうけい} — sight, spectacle (emphasizes what is visually witnessed)
- {風景|ふうけい} — landscape, scenery (natural or outdoor views)
